statement: DNA Calc is one workbook with five views (Classic, Inspector, Notebook, Model map, and App) plus Formula Explorer as a tool beside any view and as a standalone application, sharing one active selection and one edit history with Classic always one click away.
why: Modernisation is better access to the same Excel model: addresses never disappear, edits have visible destinations, and every result traces back to its source.

statement: Keep the meaning; improve the reading: every result, error, reference, spill, circular calculation, or external dependency must survive presentation unchanged, and readability never justifies silently rewriting a formula.
why: Preserves calculation fidelity and user trust across views.

statement: Protect practiced gestures: Classic adopts a documented Windows Excel keyboard and mouse baseline (not Microsoft's artwork), new commands use Alt+Q command search rather than stealing established shortcuts, and browser conflicts are disclosed with clickable and keyboard alternatives.
why: Preserves spreadsheet speed and muscle memory for experienced users.

statement: Show the source at the moment of consequence: every editable value exposes its destination before commitment, every summary exposes its coverage and omissions, and a missing observation is labelled 'not observed' rather than invented.
why: Prevents hidden edits, false completeness, and fabricated explanations.

statement: Keep context through movement: selection, sheet, formula draft, and navigation history survive a view change while each view remembers its own camera and scroll position, revealing the selected item without resetting the whole view.
why: Eliminates disorientation when moving between views.

statement: Spend attention deliberately: dense controls support hands while quiet paper supports reading; calculation, freshness, errors, and external sources use distinct words and symbols, and motion carries evidence and stops under reduced motion.
why: Avoids visual clutter and ensures status distinctions remain accessible.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Retain Strand's petrol chrome (#193F49), mist paper, teal structure, amber attention, green freshness, orange external provenance, red errors, squared cells, 5 px chips, 9 px cards, two densities, and 120-160 ms settle range, using Recursive, Recursive Mono, and Source Serif 4 packaged with open Noto/DejaVu fallbacks instead of Microsoft font fallbacks.
why: Maintains Strand visual coherence while removing proprietary Microsoft font dependencies.

statement: Refine amber into an inner accent paired with a dark contrasting outer focus stroke (since amber alone fails contrast on white), distinguish hover/selection/keyboard-focus/editing by outlines, brackets, caret, and labels, meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast with non-colour labels and click alternatives to dragging, define 'fresh' as calculated for this revision (not audited), and preserve workbook formatting including red negatives and conditional formats.
why: Meets WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility and prevents application chrome from overwriting workbook formatting.

statement: The shared shell always exposes file, sheet, view selector, command search, source address, undo, and a calculation/status strip (which Inspector panels borrow without inventing another navigation language), plus a once-dismissible, Help-restorable first-use hint: 'Same workbook. Choose a view for the task. Alt+Q finds any command.'
why: Keeps orientation and core commands constant across every view and panel.

statement: Workbook engine capabilities are accepted from the brief rather than independently certified, the five named workbooks are concrete designed fixtures (not extracted Enron files), and all timings are proposed acceptance targets rather than measured benchmarks.
why: Prevents design specifications and targets from being mistaken for completed implementation evidence.

statement: Opening Inherited.xlsm shows the shell and last saved viewport before analysis finishes without running disabled macros (LegacyClose) or refreshing missing links (Rates2024.xlsx); navigation lists sheets immediately with a separate hidden-sheet count (listing hidden names never unhides them), saved results stay labelled saved/not-current, and opening/missing-link refusal offers Locate file / Keep saved values / Cancel without a modal questionnaire.
why: Keeps large macro/broken-link workbooks immediately inspectable and safe on open.
evidence: S01; Inherited.xlsm 40 sheets, 300,000 formulas, 6 hidden, Rates2024.xlsx

statement: Workbook overview opens in the right panel (becoming a drawer at 200% zoom) showing incremental progress ('18/40 sheets inspected; 14 errors found so far') before final counts, listing dense regions as navigation entries rather than illegible cells; Ctrl+G and Back navigate across sheets, hover and keyboard 'Inspect name' preview name definitions without moving selection, and status announces completion politely once.
why: Lets analysts orient in 300k-formula workbooks without blocking or flooding screen readers.
evidence: S01; shell ≤100 ms, first saved cells ≤1 s, nav ≤50 ms p95

statement: Inspecting Summary!F18 keeps selection/address/back-path intact, runs local calculation despite the missing external file (recording that limitation), shows #REF! traced to Revenue.Window (=OFFSET(Revenue!#REF!,0,0,12,1)) separately from both the saved 2,401,300 reading and the missing external workbook, labels the graph 'Dependency explanation; execution not recorded', never guesses a repair or replaces missing data with zero, and supports Esc to discard name-edit drafts.
why: Separates local formula errors from missing external links and prevents guessed fixes.

statement: Unhiding a normally hidden sheet declares 'Model change: sheet visibility' (reversible with Ctrl+Z from either view) while protected/very-hidden sheets disclose restrictions without bypassing them; Copy evidence puts a structured text table on the clipboard, pasting annotations previews 'Presentation text, no cell change', Model map refuses 'Expand all cells' on 300,000 formulas with sheet/block/result alternatives, and crash recovery previews recovered edit addresses before restoring.
why: Protects workbook structure, provides text-based audit exports, bounds map rendering, and makes recovery safe.
evidence: S02; 300,000 formulas map refusal; nested dependency list for keyboard users

statement: Opening Notebook on a workbook without a saved layout offers the user's current selection ('Start with selected cells: Monthly!B8:M11' with Insert linked table / Start with heading / Choose other cells) rather than generic templates, distinguishing presentation insertion from Create formula (which asks for a backing cell), and supports inserting existing workbook charts as live linked objects.
why: Grounds new notebooks immediately in real workbook selections without duplicating models or charts.

statement: Notebook prose combines ordinary text with inline live fields added via Insert value (e.g., Inputs!B2, Inputs!B3, Summary!B4): a small link mark appears on focus showing the field's source cell, Done commits prose edits, and Escape cancels an uncommitted text draft.
why: Keeps reading prose clean while revealing live-value provenance on focus and protecting drafts with Escape.

statement: Budget's director Notebook presents live bound prose numbers, linked tables preserving headings/formats/source ranges, an explicitly labelled compact month summary ('Apr-Dec 162,000' with 'Open all 12 months', never silently truncated), and the workbook's chart; Tab visits cards in reading order, Enter enters tables, F2 edits source cells, Esc steps out cleanly, Move item provides a keyboard/click alternative to dragging, and layout Undo leaves workbook formulas untouched.
why: Delivers an accessible, durable live write-up backed directly by spreadsheet cells.

statement: Editing a linked cell in Notebook shows destination before commit ('Inputs!B3: 120 -> 125') and labels dependent cards 'previous revision; recalculating' until the new revision completes; Formula lens exposes readable structure and expandable LET/LAMBDA bindings without rewriting =B8-B9-B10 or creating names, Add formula previews spill footprint and occupied blockers, #SPILL! stays real with Reveal blocker / Move note... (using ordinary move semantics + Undo/Redo), and spill children are never independently editable.
why: Combines live editing, safe formula reading, and honest dynamic-array spill recovery.
evidence: S05; Budget Monthly!B11 =B8-B9-B10, Summary!A20 #SPILL! blocked by A21

statement: Copying a Notebook card frame within the workbook pastes a second live view labelled 'Linked to Summary!B7' while selecting its value copies spreadsheet content; Copy report excerpt exports rich text+table with revision/time footer for Word, Copy cells exports ordinary cells for Excel, cross-workbook linked-item paste asks for an existing binding or cell copy (never silently creating external links), Pipeline layout reflows vertically at 200% zoom, and printing waits for calculation or labels a saved snapshot.
why: Keeps clipboard semantics predictable across apps and avoids accidental cross-workbook links.

statement: Inspector explains a plausible wrong numeric result (Sales Report!B5 = 128,450 vs Paid 124,250) by evaluating all 25,000 Orders rows (not a visible sample), isolating row 10482 / worksheet row 10483 (SO10482, 4,200 Pending), framing the label mismatch as a suggestion to confirm (never inferring business rules from prose), previewing the exact one-formula repair (+Orders[Status],"Paid", diff -4,200) separately from current value before Apply, refusing stale Pivot caches as confirmation, and supporting locked-cell refusal, Copy evidence, filtered-table paste preview, and paged/virtual 25,000-row tables instead of 25,000 graph nodes.
why: Diagnoses semantic spreadsheet bugs over complete data with honest confirmation and reversible repair.
evidence: S06, S07; Sales Report!B5, Orders!A10483:G10483, 25,000 rows

statement: Model map requires sheet cells for every new input or calculation block ('New model items need sheet cells', creating ordinary labels/cells and optional aliases rather than hidden name formulas); wiring draws a ghost line for a pending edit and previews the exact before/after formula and operand change (Stock!H15 adding $B$5+ to threshold, result 0 -> 420) with full keyboard/click parity (Connect to...), refusing ambiguous multi-operand/opaque targets by opening F2 candidate selection, deleting nodes as presentation-only by default, and requiring explicit reference replacement on wire deletion rather than substituting zero.
why: Keeps visual model building strictly grounded in real worksheet cells and exact formula edits.

statement: Stock's circular reserve (B8 =0.5*(B8+B7)) requires explicit iteration settings (max 100, change 0.001, reviewing affected workbook/session scope) and appears on the map as 'circular group; iteration enabled' distinct from the 3-day row-based lag (H15 day 2 -> C18 day 5); the workbook's native form-control slider links to B5 (increment 10, keyboard/pointer Undo), non-converging preview (=B8+1) runs in a temporary copy of workbook state reporting real stop reason or 'Convergence status unavailable' (never green verified), and map image copies include scope, iteration settings, and timestamp.
why: Prevents conflating circular convergence with time delays and guarantees honest cycle testing.

statement: Loan opens in preferred view 'App: Loan comparison' bound directly to Loan!B2:B4 and B6:B7 (missing layout falls back to Classic/Restore without inventing an app); inputs mark drafts with a star and text (revealing source addresses on focus or Source rather than cluttering every ordinary label), enforce workbook Stop validation (term 1..360) without overwriting applied results, batch edits until Apply inputs (Discard clears all, Esc reverts focused field), label prior results during recalc, keep 'Compare last applied inputs' as a recorded observation (distinct from Save scenario... creating an Excel Scenario Manager record), keep recovered drafts unapplied after restart, and print a one-page proof with optional full 360-row schedule and wait-vs-previous calculation choice.
why: Delivers a calm operator form over real Excel cells with strict draft/applied separation and honest printing.

statement: Standalone DNA Calc - Formula Explorer has no workbook, sheet tabs, or hidden temporary workbook: users explicitly review and load add-ins per session, run Evaluate on literal-argument expressions with number-format and context-free conditional-format testing, verify expected errors (#NUM! matches as a passing test while keeping #NUM! visible), receive plain tool-status refusal for caller-dependent functions (DNA.CALLERADDRESS()) and desktop-host/equivalent routes for unavailable native XLLs, and when docked beside Budget's Summary!D14 test trials in isolation until Apply (with real caller context, F6 region cycling, cancellable UDF progress, and exact Copy formula/test results).
why: Supports safe add-in and formula testing both standalone (skin 0) and docked to a real cell without faking workbook context.
evidence: S12, S13; DiscountFunctions.xll 1.0, DNA.DISCOUNT, DNA.CALLERADDRESS, Budget Summary!D14

statement: Tools > Agent discloses its scope and requires explicit provider data-sharing permission (never granted by a workbook or skin), runs non-blockingly without seizing focus (Stop retains an incomplete unapplied proposal), and presents proposals as discrete review units separating Model changes, Presentation changes, and unsupported suggestions; ticking units is inert, Review selected computes exact subset previews and scoped changed-cell counts, structurally dependent edits (e.g., creating and using a name) cannot be half-accepted, bulk edits show counts plus all exceptions, and diffs reserve red for errors (using Before/After + strike/underline).
why: Keeps AI-assisted workbook changes transparent, scoped, non-intrusive, and reviewable unit by unit.
evidence: S14; Budget P17 A (price 120->125, 24 cells), B (heading), C (cost 70->72 unsupported)

statement: Applying selected agent units validates all of them atomically against the base revision yet records separate ordered Undo units (A then B) so one Ctrl+Z reverts B while keeping A; History keeps full attribution even after Undo/Reject (Undo never deletes the audit record, and Redo restores B until a new edit invalidates that redo branch), view navigation never consumes Undo, stale base values (expected 120, current 123, proposed 125) block conflicting units without overwriting while letting independent units proceed (Recompute refreshes preview), reverting an older edit after later work uses 'Create reversal' (a checked new proposal rather than arbitrary selective undo), external macro side effects are marked non-undoable, and restart recovery never replays accepted edits twice or auto-applies pending proposals.
why: Provides atomic acceptance, stepwise reversibility, audit attribution, and conflict safety across human-agent work.

statement: Conceptual target 'Cell / range': Original sheet coordinates and Excel selection rules. A multi-area selection retains its active cell. A cell edit changes workbook content.
why: Defines unambiguous user targets and their editing consequences across all views.

statement: Conceptual target 'Block': A view grouping of an explicit member set, perhaps discontiguous. Expanding lists members and exceptions. Grouping alone creates no formula, name or new scope.
why: Defines unambiguous user targets and their editing consequences across all views.

statement: Conceptual target 'Name': A real workbook- or sheet-scoped identifier referring to cells, a constant or a formula. Scope and evaluation context stay visible; dotted text is not an extra namespace. [S9]
why: Defines unambiguous user targets and their editing consequences across all views.

statement: Conceptual target 'Table / array': A real Table with headers/rows, or an array with an anchor and shape. Presentation sorting/filtering never silently changes source order or formulas.
why: Defines unambiguous user targets and their editing consequences across all views.

statement: Conceptual target 'Object': The actual workbook chart, shape, form control or other supported object. A view item may reference it; copying the view is distinct from duplicating the object.
why: Defines unambiguous user targets and their editing consequences across all views.

statement: Conceptual target 'View item': A card, paragraph, group, port, binding or panel arrangement. It may have one source, several sources, or none for prose. Its identity is not a cell address.
why: Defines unambiguous user targets and their editing consequences across all views.

statement: Every selection carries a source, active member, and optional presentation item displayed plainly in the address field (e.g., Summary!B7, Orders[Amount], Workbook::Stock.ReorderPoint, or Notebook paragraph), while commands accepting Excel addresses continue accepting standard Excel syntax without inserting UI scope labels into formulas.
why: Unifies selection identity across grid cells, tables, names, and source-less prose.

statement: View preference is sheet-local unless a workbook-wide map or overview is open (with scope explicitly named); switching sheets restores that sheet's preferred or last-used view and source position, explicit user choices override file defaults, and Classic always remains available.
why: Supports mixed per-sheet views without surprising global view switches.

statement: When switching views, if the selected source is absent from the destination layout the UI shows 'Selected source is not in this layout' with 'Reveal in Classic' and 'Add to this view' (never manufacturing a substitute selection); source-less paragraphs keep their view selection while remembering the last model cell separately, and active formula drafts stay in an anchored editor or defer the view switch with Commit/Cancel choices without implicit commits.
why: Preserves selection integrity and uncommitted edits across view transitions.

statement: Every non-grid editor distinguishes Model change from Presentation change before commitment, respects sheet protection, saved validation rules/alert styles, and macro security without silently altering validation behavior, discloses all affected sheets for grouped-sheet edits, and never hides Classic.
why: Enforces one consistent editing and protection contract across every view.

statement: Selection determines ordinary copy (cells copy Excel-compatible cells with source origin; text copies text; view-item frames copy presentation inside this workbook), Copy formula text copies exact source with origin disclosed, paste previews name the target type and refuse ambiguous external bindings, and Formula lens formatting never silently becomes executable clipboard syntax.
why: Keeps copy/paste faithful to Excel and avoids hidden external links or lens-syntax leakage.

statement: Each workbook has one ordered undo history covering both reversible model edits and authored-presentation changes; navigation and transient panel/camera changes use Back/Forward instead of Undo, local draft undo operates inside active editors before commit, and recovery distinguishes committed edits from unapplied drafts.
why: Prevents view-dependent undo confusion and keeps navigation out of edit history.

statement: Workbook and cell states are strictly orthogonal: loading/ready, clean/dirty/calculating/cancelled, current/saved/previous, source connected/stale/missing, and error/no error; Excel formula errors stay real cell values rather than replacement app statuses, live panels show source time, receipt time, revision, and retained-history coverage with pause-observation separate from stopping a feed, and Inspector shows observed execution only when supplied.
why: Prevents conflating calculation state, freshness, connection status, and Excel error values.

statement: Classic is the precision workspace retaining A1/R1C1, name box, formula bar, sheet tabs, freeze panes, range selection, fill/drag, and compact text-led command bands with original icons (Page Layout, Review, and Developer reachable via More, key tips, and Alt+Q); the caret indicates editing rather than a second app mode, F2 toggles Edit vs Point, F4 anchors the active reference token, and Classic never declines any workbook.
why: Provides complete Excel-familiar precision editing as the universal fallback view.

statement: Inspector provides Precedents, Dependents, Calculation, and Live tabs over a selected source, presenting the same dependency scope as both list and graph (arrows select, Right expands, Left collapses, Enter reveals source, Back restores trace), separating observed execution traces from dependency order, reporting Pivot cache freshness independently of formulas, prompting on empty selection, and starting whole-workbook inspection with counts rather than a graph explosion.
why: Delivers evidence-first auditing and phyphox-style separation of readings from instrument state.

statement: Notebook presents a live explanation in deliberate reading order (vertical or horizontal Pipeline, neither altering calculation order), borrowing Pluto's reactive reading feel while preserving Excel's manual-calculation, reference, and scope rules; table/array cards support labelled view filters, row windows, and export (keeping actual Excel Table filter edits separate), and a blank notebook invites content selection rather than implying an empty workbook.
why: Combines reactive reading narrative with full Excel calculation and Table fidelity.

statement: Model map displays inspectable blocks, ports with larger hit areas, a Connections list alternative, hierarchy groups (Enter opens, breadcrumb/Back exits), distinct lag labels vs circular-iteration enclosures, and inspectable dynamic INDEX ranges (distinguishing full possible range from selected precedent); mouse wheel scrolls canvas while explicit Zoom/Fit and Ctrl+wheel zoom without stealing ordinary scroll, and recurring schedules (like Loan's 360 rows) appear as expandable period recurrence blocks.
why: Visualizes system structure cleanly while staying accessible and bounded at scale.

statement: App presents an uncluttered authored form following authored Tab order with accessible Source actions on results, committing pending input drafts together via Apply inputs (Esc cancels focused field, Discard clears pending set), and declining automatic publication for unstructured workbooks like Inherited until an author confirms an input/output contract.
why: Gives operational users a focused, validated interface without detaching from Classic.

statement: Docked Formula Explorer opens beside a cell (Explore formula) capturing its source revision, inputs, formatting, and real caller context; trial evaluation refuses to silently run side-effecting macros/UDFs (requiring explicit execution or refusing preview), stale callers require refresh before Apply, F6 cycles regions, and it stays a focused formula tool rather than a second whole-workbook editor.
why: Enables safe in-context formula debugging without side effects or stale overwrites.

statement: Standalone Formula Explorer evaluates built-ins, add-ins, errors, arrays, number formats, and context-free conditional-format rules with explicit Evaluate for unknown/external providers (safe built-ins may preview while typing with a draft label), saves test files with provider requirements rather than disguised .xlsx files, and never substitutes font/colour previews for the underlying result value.
why: Provides a lightweight workbook-free formula and formatting laboratory.

statement: Recognise workbook structure (Tables, chart sources, form controls, formula references) before business meaning, using four explicit interpretation states — From workbook, Suggested, Confirmed by Maria, and Needs review after change — with no invented confidence percentages; confirmation records who confirmed what without turning intent inference into calculation fact, and structural edits invalidate only the interpretation, not the workbook.
why: Prevents speculative semantic labels from masquerading as workbook facts.

statement: Pattern family 'Database and references': Sales' Orders Table is explicit; key uniqueness and Paid-only intent require evidence. Confirm row/header ranges, keys and lookup modes. Recommended first presentation: Classic for editing; Inspector for contributions; Notebook/App for bounded tables; one map node per table.
why: Maps recurring spreadsheet structures to appropriate views and confirmation steps.

statement: Pattern family 'Assumptions and scenarios': Budget's labelled Base/Stretch columns suggest scenarios. Confirm cells, units and comparison outputs; preserve validation/protection. Recommended first presentation: Notebook for explanation, App for operation, Classic for bulk edits; map inputs remain cell-bound.
why: Maps recurring spreadsheet structures to appropriate views and confirmation steps.

statement: Pattern family 'Repeated calculation and time': Monthly has twelve repeated columns; Loan has 360 period rows. Show seeds, relative patterns and exceptions. Recommended first presentation: Classic keeps geometry; Inspector compares formulas; map uses a run/block; Notebook/App show labelled excerpts and full data access.
why: Maps recurring spreadsheet structures to appropriate views and confirmation steps.

statement: Pattern family 'Systems and feedback': Stock's arrivals refer to earlier order rows; reserve is a genuine circular calculation. Confirm units and intended loop. Recommended first presentation: Model map distinguishes lag, recurrence and iteration; Inspector exposes each exact source.
why: Maps recurring spreadsheet structures to appropriate views and confirmation steps.

statement: Pattern family 'Execution and external state': Macros, RTD, external links, random functions and data tables are actual mechanisms, but do not prove their business purpose. Recommended first presentation: Inspector shows observed state; other views display relevant source/permission/freshness notices.
why: Maps recurring spreadsheet structures to appropriate views and confirmation steps.

statement: Pattern family 'Reporting and controls': Existing print areas, charts, pivot objects and linked controls provide candidates. Author confirms reading order and input/output contract. Recommended first presentation: Notebook for a report; App for a constrained interaction; Classic remains the complete source.
why: Maps recurring spreadsheet structures to appropriate views and confirmation steps.

statement: Pattern correction exposes 'Why suggested' evidence, retains hard-coded overrides as explicit exceptions rather than removing them, limits Split block / Change heading row / Include cells / 'This is not a time series' to presentation metadata (never auto-converting ranges to Excel Tables), surfaces unclassified islands as labelled ranges with a Classic preview, never auto-promotes unconfirmed assumptions to App, and keeps hidden sheets hidden in the inventory.
why: Keeps structural interpretation non-destructive, auditable, and respectful of irregular spreadsheets.

statement: Sampling is an explicit tool (e.g., 'Sample: 200 of 25,000 rows, selected evenly by row position') distinct from full contribution calculations and virtualised displays, never used as the basis for exact totals or soundness claims; every condensed formula run shows member count, bounds, and exception count, and the Enron corpus (16,189 unique / 15,770 analyzable files, 20,277,835 formula cells) motivates irregular-workbook testing without standing in for modern features.
why: Prevents sampled inspections from being misreported as exact complete audits.

statement: For large workbooks, 'everything is available' does not mean 'everything is drawn at once': opening, navigating, analysing, and calculating must maintain separate progress and cancellation so one expensive step never stalls the others.
why: Keeps enterprise-scale workbooks responsive across heterogeneous workloads.

statement: Big-workbook rule for Classic: Every cell/object remains addressable; draw the viewport. Preserve hidden/filter/freeze meanings. An unloaded region says Loading, not blank. Dense formatting alone does not imply dense data. A failure identifies the unavailable region and keeps the original file intact.
why: Defines exact simplify and honest-refusal behaviour per view at scale.

statement: Big-workbook rule for Inspector: Begin at the selected result, one dependency frontier. Group repeated formulas and cycles; show known/unknown edges and exact member/exception counts. Above 200 visible nodes or 400 edges, offer block/list form. Refuse “draw every dependency” with scope-preserving alternatives.
why: Defines exact simplify and honest-refusal behaviour per view at scale.

statement: Big-workbook rule for Notebook: Render the saved narrative, or an empty selected-content page. Virtualise large tables; show window/total counts. Refuse “make a paragraph for every cell”; offer blocks, a selected range or a report. Unplaced workbook content remains in the inventory.
why: Defines exact simplify and honest-refusal behaviour per view at scale.

statement: Big-workbook rule for Model map: Start with sheet groups, then blocks. Auto-layout at most 200 expanded nodes/400 edges per viewport; budgets are defaults, not data deletion. Beyond this show boundary ports and counted collapsed groups. Expansion opens a focused submap with breadcrumb.
why: Defines exact simplify and honest-refusal behaviour per view at scale.

statement: Big-workbook rule for App: Render the authored input/output contract. A missing layout says `No App is defined. Open Classic / Choose inputs and outputs`. A broken binding shows Source missing; it never silently substitutes a nearby cell. Unknown calculation/runtime dependencies remain visible.
why: Defines exact simplify and honest-refusal behaviour per view at scale.

statement: Benchmark responsiveness on a proposed reference environment (Windows 11, 4 modern CPU cores, 16 GB RAM, local SSD, 1440×900, current browser, fixed checksummed Inherited fixture) plus a constrained 8 GB / 200%-400% zoom profile reported separately, using 10 cold opens and ≥1,000 input actions with p50/p95/p99, hardware, bytes, cache, and provider state recorded; crossing a budget is a performance failure (never permission to omit data), save/export stays cancellable without corrupting last-good files, and screen-reader announcements coalesce while preserving real virtualised coordinates.
why: Sets reproducible performance and accessibility measurement standards for large workbooks.

statement: Experience budget 'Open acknowledgement / shell first paint': ≤100 ms / ≤300 ms p95 after Open is accepted.
why: Sets measurable responsiveness acceptance targets on the reference environment.

statement: Experience budget 'First useful viewport': ≤1 s p95, saved values labelled; do not wait for full dependency analysis.
why: Sets measurable responsiveness acceptance targets on the reference environment.

statement: Experience budget 'Interactive sheet inventory / coarse block overview': ≤2 s / ≤5 s p95; incomplete counts and scope visible while processing.
why: Sets measurable responsiveness acceptance targets on the reference environment.

statement: Experience budget 'Keystroke to visible caret/selection': ≤50 ms p95, ≤100 ms p99 during background load/recalc.
why: Sets measurable responsiveness acceptance targets on the reference environment.

statement: Experience budget 'Local view switch with known source': ≤150 ms p95 for continuity feedback; bounded content ≤500 ms or an explicit loading state.
why: Sets measurable responsiveness acceptance targets on the reference environment.

statement: Experience budget 'Cancellation': Acknowledge ≤100 ms; return control ≤500 ms where cancellable. Identify an uninterruptible provider instead of claiming it stopped.
why: Sets measurable responsiveness acceptance targets on the reference environment.

statement: Experience budget 'Panning / visible live-value delivery': Aim 60 Hz; apply a received calculated revision within 100 ms p95 without forcing every intermediate event to render.
why: Sets measurable responsiveness acceptance targets on the reference environment.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: A skin is a declaration over a fixed interaction contract (theme tokens, density, view layouts, source bindings, reading/tab order, panels, command placements, keymaps, print layouts); themes must obey Strand contrast rules and cannot recolour errors into success or suppress stale notices, custom keymaps are named/previewable and explicitly leave Classic conformance, and every command keeps a named shell route.
why: Allows rich visual and layout customisation without undermining legibility or discoverability.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: The immutable core forbidden to skins comprises address/source identity, formula meaning, calculation state, workbook permission/security, protected commands, truthful error/status presentation, clipboard semantics, and review/undo rules; custom components may render or request supported actions but cannot embed a hidden calculation engine or secret input transforms, require add-in-grade host review, and are never authorised merely by opening a workbook.
why: Protects single-evaluator integrity and security boundaries against custom skins and components.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: 'View > Edit this layout' edits the current layout declaration as an inspectable draft with live preview and built-in keyboard/contrast checks: 'Try in this window' affects only preview, 'Use for this workbook' saves a presentation transaction (with Undo), 'Export skin' writes a versioned package without workbook values by default, Import discloses commands/components/unavailable bindings, and broken bindings stay visibly broken without approximate-address fallback.
why: Makes skin authoring, testing, and sharing safe, reversible, and free of accidental data leaks.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Worked example: an agent restyles Classic (keeping Working density, 15.5 px formula text, 320 px right Inspector, cockpit-light, Classic keymap unchanged) via a side-by-side preview computing 'Changes: presentation only; 0 cells, formulas or names' from the actual diff, rejecting drafts that clip the address or fail contrast, preserving F2/F4/Ctrl+Enter/fill-handle behaviour, and reverting as one Ctrl+Z presentation edit.
why: Illustrates safe agent-assisted presentation customisation checked against layout and contrast rules.

topic: XII. Customisation and the skin API
statement: Worked example: from a three-line prompt, the agent first proposes exact Loan bindings (B2:B4 writable inputs, B6:B7 outputs, existing balance chart, A12:F371 schedule) reusing workbook units/validation without ever creating a second PMT calculation; after testing edits, invalid term, tab order, 200% zoom, source jump, and print proof, accepting stores the App layout only while any new Excel validation or scenario records appear as separate model changes.
why: Illustrates agent-built Apps constrained strictly to workbook bindings and one evaluator.

statement: Store versioned, optional view declarations in the workbook's custom-XML presentation part using both stable binding identities and human-readable addresses, validate identities after external edits (an A1 address surviving does not prove the same target survived), prompt review/rebinding on uncertain bindings, fall back to Classic with export-restore if a cleaner removes the part, and treat view preferences as preferences rather than a way to hide Classic or force code execution.
why: Balances portable in-file view persistence with resilience against external edits and Document Inspector stripping.

statement: Every view prints a fixed, labelled calculation revision: Classic honours workbook print areas/breaks/titles/scaling/charts; Notebook prints reading order (paginating pipelines vertically); Inspector prints evidence, formulas, scope, and omitted branches; Model map prints a selected hierarchy/region with boundary connectors and index (never shrinking dense graphs into illegibility); App prints its authored report plus explicitly selected schedule pages; Formula Explorer prints expression, inputs, caller, provider/version, expected/observed tests, and formatting rules.
why: Ensures every view produces honest, legible, scope-disclosed printouts.

statement: Print preview explicitly labels Current / Previous / Saved results, timestamp, filters, and missing sources while keeping errors as errors; Excel export preserves actual model content and supported presentation metadata, PDF is a frozen report, and converting macro workbooks to macro-free formats requires an explicit content-loss choice.
why: Prevents stale or unlabelled printouts and silent macro stripping on export.

statement: Macros may select cells, request an existing view, and show panels through optional capability-checked presentation commands (with Classic selection revealing the same source, documented no-op/fallback when unsupported, and unavailable execution reported before running); calculation macros must never depend on DNA-only view calls to work in Excel, calculation mode is never silently changed for a view, macro trust applies in every view including App buttons, and macro code is preserved even on hosts that cannot execute it.
why: Supports view-aware VBA automation while maintaining Excel compatibility and uniform security.

statement: Document changes from a macro are grouped where capturable; before non-undoable actions the UI names the limitation and offers a recoverable workbook checkpoint while keeping external side effects outside document undo, history records only observed effects, and macro-driven focus changes are announced and recorded in navigation history without hiding destinations.
why: Sets honest boundaries for macro undo, history attribution, and focus tracking.

statement: Push-back 1: A circular reference is not automatically a time delay. Reserve time-delay labels for explicit prior-period references or an established workbook mechanism (using Stock's day rows for the 3-day lag and a separate iteration enclosure for B8), keeping hierarchy, port values, source toggle, parameter rail, and click-to-inspect from the HTML sketches while omitting ungrounded per-group 'directors' and JS-imposed snapshot semantics from Names in Motion / Watershed.
why: JavaScript snapshot/settling loops in sketches do not establish that Excel circular formulas act as time delays.

statement: Push-back 2: A dependency picture is not an execution recording. Label graph animations 'Dependency explanation', show 'Observed execution' only when the host genuinely reports it (preserving partial order / concurrent bands rather than fabricating a serial order), and default to static or simultaneous change highlights when only before/after values are known.
why: Excel dynamically revises its calculation chain and evaluates independent regions concurrently.

statement: Push-back 3: Formula lens must not become automatic formula refactoring. Introducing shared LET bindings can alter evaluation multiplicity (e.g., RAND()+RAND() != LET(r,RAND(),r+r)), scope, @ implicit intersection, spill #, coercion, and error behaviour; default to faithful structure/aliases and offer 'Rewrite formula' only as an explicit proposed model change without claiming single-input parity proves universal equivalence.
why: Silent algebraic or LET rewriting can break Excel calculation semantics.

statement: Push-back 4: 'Excel ignores and keeps it' needs an explicit tested save-route matrix rather than a blanket promise, because Document Inspector, format conversions, privacy cleaners, and third-party editors can remove custom XML; promise retention on tested routes plus graceful fallback and recovery when stripped.
why: Makes the in-file persistence guarantee technically accurate and testable.

statement: Push-back 5: Preserving a file intact does not imply every macro, XLL, or caller-dependent runtime works on every host. Distinguish file preservation from provider/caller/host availability, never secretly create a workbook in standalone Explorer or substitute a different implementation in App, and route users directly to a capable host.
why: Prevents cross-platform compatibility promises from obscuring native runtime limits.

statement: Explicitly rejected alternatives: (1) keeping six experimental views as top-level modes (fold ledger/atlas/tree/canvas into the five views); (2) a separate visual-programming runtime; (3) run-once script notebook cells; (4) automatic App publication from inference; (5) per-view undo stacks; (6) hiding Classic for managers; (7) a full Microsoft Excel ribbon reskin (keep interaction structure in Strand's compact command bands without Microsoft assets).
why: Keeps the product coherent around five views, one Excel evaluator, one undo history, and Strand aesthetics.

statement: The top three design risks are: (1) a convincing interface that overstates what it knows, (2) disrupting practiced Excel editing, and (3) coupling five presentations so tightly that one expensive analysis stalls all work; therefore source/state honesty, Classic conformance, and bounded presentation must be primary acceptance criteria from the start.
why: Prioritises structural integrity over visual polish.

statement: Owner decision — Which Excel interaction/version profile is the acceptance oracle? Recommendation: Use a pinned current Microsoft 365 Windows desktop build for Classic gestures, with a separately named legacy profile only where needed. Record locale, keyboard and settings. Calculation compatibility and file targets remain separate contracts.
why: Resolves key cross-cutting product policy questions explicitly.

statement: Owner decision — Can circular calculations be drawn without implying time delays? Recommendation: Approve the explicit §10 qualification: feedback enclosure for iteration; period-labelled delay only when backed by model evidence. Keep the actual Excel mechanisms.
why: Resolves key cross-cutting product policy questions explicitly.

statement: Owner decision — What execution evidence and host capabilities can be exposed reliably? Recommendation: Make changed values, runtime reads, true calculation trace, convergence and provider availability separately discoverable. Require honest `Unavailable / Not observed` states; do not block basic views on optional diagnostics.
why: Resolves key cross-cutting product policy questions explicitly.

statement: Owner decision — Which file/save routes retain presentation and which histories travel? Recommendation: First certify ordinary `.xlsx` and macro-preserving `.xlsm` routes on named desktop/web Excel versions. Save authored layouts and accepted-change provenance; keep transient undo/recovery local unless explicitly exported. Permit a privacy choice for provenance.
why: Resolves key cross-cutting product policy questions explicitly.

statement: Owner decision — How much independent work may an agent perform? Recommendation: Default to proposal-and-review for model writes, allow explicitly delegated scopes, and always show attributed source changes. Presentation drafts can be previewed freely; accepting them cannot grant provider, macro or external data access.
why: Resolves key cross-cutting product policy questions explicitly.

statement: Run the same five cast fixtures plus screen-reader, zoom, and Enron-derived stress checks across every completed view rather than isolated per-view demos; design completion requires that a reviewer can identify the backing cell/object for every non-prose item, predict every edit and undo, distinguish current results from stored observations, and switch to Classic without losing their place.
why: Ensures real cross-view coherence before visual embellishment.

statement: Classic keyboard/mouse acceptance uses a pinned Excel for Microsoft 365 Windows English/US build as oracle (locale-specific fixtures separately, never silently importing Mac/Web/2010/OS-reserved behavior, with no Microsoft icons/artwork); input routing strictly follows focused editor/menu/dialog → focused view → shell (disabled commands state why rather than acting differently), and Ctrl+F2 follows current Microsoft docs as formula-bar editing (not Print Preview; Ctrl+P always prints).
why: Eliminates ambiguous shortcut routing and outdated Excel profile collisions.

statement: A-01 [Alt or F10, no editor active]: Show key tips on the compact command strip; no model or selection change. Esc removes tips and restores prior focus.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-02 [Key-tip letters]: Follow the displayed path; show the remaining valid letters. Preserve familiar group initials F/File, H/Home, N/Insert, P/Page Layout, M/Formulas, A/Data, R/Review, W/View, L/Developer. Layout stays Strand.

statement: A-03 [Common key-tip sequences]: Support Alt,H,V,V (paste values), Alt,H,O,I (autofit columns), Alt,H,O,R (rename sheet), Alt,A,T (toggle filter), Alt,W,F,F (freeze panes); test each against the named baseline. Sequence is not a simultaneous chord.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-04 [Legacy Alt,E,S,V,Enter]: Paste values through Paste Special. Legacy paths are aliases, shown in command search; unknown paths do not guess a command.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-05 [F6 / Shift+F6]: Cycle view, command strip, open panels and status/zoom landmarks forward/backward; preserve the last focus inside each. Split panes are reachable.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-06 [Tab / Shift+Tab in controls]: Traverse controls in reading order; do not move the underlying active cell. In a composite list, arrow keys move its items.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-07 [Shift+F10 or Menu key]: Open the same contextual actions as right-click for the focused cell, block, object or sheet tab. Esc returns to that exact target.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-08 [F1; Ctrl+F1]: Open contextual help; show/hide the command strip, respectively. Neither obscures the current edit without retaining it.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-09 [Click a cell; Shift+click another]: Select one cell; extend a rectangle from the selection anchor. Expose address, dimensions, active cell and error state to assistive technology.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-10 [Drag through cells]: Grow a rectangular selection; scroll at viewport edges; show final dimensions before release. Dragging cell interior is distinct from dragging its border.

statement: A-15 [End then Arrow]: Enter the visible End-navigation state and move to its next boundary; a completed movement clears that state.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-16 [Page Up/Down; Alt+Page Up/Down]: Move one viewport vertically/horizontally, preserving approximate relative position; frozen areas remain frozen.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-17 [Ctrl+Page Up/Down]: Previous/next worksheet in workbook order. Skip hidden sheets as Excel does; restore each sheet's own selection and scroll position.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-18 [Ctrl+Shift+Page Up/Down]: Extend grouped-sheet selection. Show a persistent Grouped sheets label and the affected sheet count before edits.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-19 [Ctrl+Space; Shift+Space]: Select column/row in the current context. In a table, the first Ctrl+Space selects column data; the second includes the column header. Test subsequent expansion and Shift+Space against the recorded baseline. [KA3]

statement: A-20 [Ctrl+A]: In a table: data, then the entire table including headers. Outside a table: current region, then its summary rows, then worksheet where applicable. In an editor select its text, not the worksheet. [KA3]

statement: A-24 [Ctrl+.; Ctrl+Backspace]: Cycle corners of a rectangular selection; reveal active cell without collapsing selection.

statement: A-39 [Formula autocomplete]: Offer Excel functions, names, table references and loaded add-in functions; arrows choose, Tab inserts, Esc dismisses. Completion is distinct from committing the cell. [KA7]

statement: A-40 [Shift+F3; F3]: Open function argument help; insert a defined name. Empty names list explains that no names exist and offers Define name.

statement: A-41 [Type `=SUM(`, then mouse-select B4:M4]: Insert `B4:M4` at the reference insertion point; numbered outlines link text to ranges without relying on rainbow colors. Type `)` and Enter to commit. [KA8]

statement: A-42 [Pick a reference on another sheet or open workbook]: Preserve the unfinished formula and its origin; generate the correct quoted qualifier. Returning focus does not commit accidentally. External links are marked. [KA8]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-43 [Drag reference outline/corner during editing]: Change the selected reference range in the draft; preserve its absolute/relative flags; update formula text and preview together. Esc cancels the entire draft. [KA8]
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-44 [F4 with a reference active]: Cycle `A1` -> `$A$1` -> `A$1` -> `$A1` -> `A1`; selected ranges retain corresponding endpoint behavior. Structured-reference details follow observed fixtures, never a blind string rewrite. [KA6]

statement: A-47 [F9 outside editing]: Recalculate dirty formulas across open workbooks in the current session; keep last completed results explicitly stale while working. Do not refresh external sources merely because F9 was pressed.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-48 [Shift+F9; Ctrl+Alt+F9; Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F9]: Calculate active sheet; full calculation; dependency recheck plus full calculation. Show which scope was requested and cancellation state. [KA11]

statement: A-57 [Esc after copy/cut, before paste]: Cancel pending clipboard operation and source marching outline; do not erase source values. After paste use Undo.

statement: A-59 [Ctrl+Shift+V under current profile]: Paste values; show exact destination and retained number-format behavior. Older-profile or host conflicts are disclosed in shortcut settings.

why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-70 [Ctrl++ / Ctrl+-]: Insert/delete selected whole rows/columns directly; for ordinary cells ask direction of shift. Multi-area, table, protected and array conflicts explain why they cannot commit.

statement: A-73 [Right-click sheet tab; drag / Ctrl+drag tab]: Rename, move, copy, hide, unhide or delete using the shown action; Ctrl+drag creates a copy. Grouped-sheet state remains prominent.

why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: A-106 [Shortcut customization]: Show conflicts, affected contexts, baseline command and reset. Imported skins cannot override core recovery/escape or reserve a hidden action behind a familiar command.
why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

why: Normative Windows Microsoft 365 Excel Classic interaction conformance requirement.

statement: C-1: Identify a workbook, sheet, cell/range, name, table and object, and tell whether a formerly identified source still exists after edits or reopen.
why: Preserve selection and bindings without guessing nearby replacements.

statement: C-2: Read exact formulas, stored values, formatted text, number formats, styles, errors, annotations and relevant workbook settings.
why: Show source truth and preserve imported presentation.

statement: C-3: Know whether a value is saved, current, dirty, calculating, cancelled or unavailable, and which completed document revision it belongs to.
why: Prevent stale or mixed-revision results from appearing current.

statement: C-4: Be told which cells/objects/settings changed after an edit or calculation, including formatting and changed spill shape.
why: Update all bound views without re-reading the entire workbook.

statement: C-5: Read available cells incrementally, with trustworthy progress and the distinction between empty, not yet loaded and failed to load.
why: Keep Inherited usable during opening.

statement: C-6: Read sheet/table/object inventories with hidden/protection state, used extents and complete-versus-partial counts.
why: Honest navigation and large-workbook overview.

statement: C-7: Know formula precedents/dependents, summarised by range/block, with unresolved, conditional and runtime-selected references distinguished.
why: Explain Sales and Stock without fabricating connections.

statement: C-8: Obtain exact dependency membership and exceptions behind a grouped formula run or edge.
why: Expand summaries and target a precise map edit.

statement: C-9: Inspect a formula's syntactic structure, reference identity, local bindings, evaluation location and exact source spelling.
why: Render a faithful lens and safely resolve a displayed alias.

statement: C-10: Distinguish cells, spill anchors/children, legacy array regions, tables, pivot outputs, protected cells and objects when deciding editability.
why: Make every view obey the same edit rules.

statement: C-11: Preview and apply normal Excel-compatible edits with exact old/new targets, reference adjustments, validation and affected scope.
why: Share one editing contract across grid, map, notebook and agent.

statement: C-12: Apply a related set of changes atomically, reject stale expectations, and report conflicts at their actual source.
why: Prevent partial agent acceptance and stale Explorer apply.

statement: C-13: Record reversible edits and meaningful undo units across both model and authored presentation, while identifying non-reversible effects.
why: Predictable global undo and honest macro history.

statement: C-14: Retain/recover committed work and unapplied drafts distinctly, with identities sufficient to avoid repeating accepted actions.
why: Safe restart without automatic re-execution.

statement: C-15: Evaluate a formula trial in an explicit caller/input context, and distinguish expression testing from replacing a formula in temporary workbook state.
why: Ade's UDF tests and Lee's genuine cycle preview.

statement: C-16: Say whether a provider can be safely previewed, requires explicit execution, needs workbook context, or has external side effects.
why: Avoid invisible execution while typing or reviewing.

statement: C-17: Enumerate add-in functions and their available metadata, provider/version, permission state and supported execution host.
why: Honest autocomplete, loading and missing-provider paths.

statement: C-18: Expose formula-result values separately from number-format and conditional-format evaluation, including reference anchors when needed.
why: Test formatting without confusing display with calculation.

statement: C-19: Expose actual calculation mode, effective scope, iterative settings, cycle members and any genuinely observed convergence/stop reason.
why: Distinguish Stock's circular reserve from its period lag.

statement: C-20: Supply observed calculation trace/order/concurrency only when available, separately from dependency relations and value differences.
why: Avoid a fictional recalc animation.

statement: C-21: Report external link/provider identity, source availability, last supplied value/time and refresh/connection state without silently refreshing.
why: Missing sources and live instruments remain honest.

statement: C-22: Report observed live updates and their timestamps/coverage, and tell whether intermediate events were coalesced or not observed.
why: Label retained histories and avoid false event causality.

statement: C-23: Perform exact filtering/contribution queries on the requested scope and disclose incomplete processing; retrieve bounded row windows with stable source targets.
why: Sales' exact audit and large table interaction.

statement: C-24: Read and operate actual PivotTables, chart objects, form controls, scenario records, validation rules and print settings.
why: Views reuse existing workbook mechanisms.

statement: C-25: Know macro/module presence, trust, execution availability, run boundaries and observed workbook effects; support optional presentation requests.
why: Keep macro-driven models usable and attributed.

statement: C-26: Save/load versioned optional view declarations and source bindings in supported files, preserving unrelated workbook parts.
why: Make preferred views travel without changing calculation content.

statement: C-27: Detect missing/unsupported presentation versions and provide preserved declarations for recovery rather than silently throwing them away.
why: Graceful fallback to Classic.

statement: C-28: Preserve/transfer ordinary clipboard content with source-origin, formula/value/text/format distinctions and declare loss at an unsupported destination.
why: Reliable cross-view and Excel/program copy-paste.

statement: C-29: Provide a consistent completed-result snapshot and all relevant filters/source statuses for printing or report export.
why: Avoid mixed calculation revisions on paper.

statement: C-30: Expose all commands, edit states, coordinates, labels, selections and statuses through accessible interaction surfaces.
why: Keyboard, screen reader and high-zoom parity.

statement: C-31: Cancel or bound long work, report uninterruptible operations honestly, and keep ordinary navigation/edit feedback responsive.
why: Meet §6 without inventing computation completion.
